commands.description: One batched read of host, OS, the server's own IPv4 (source address of its route to the internet) and its Tailscale IPv4 (empty when Tailscale is not installed or connected), uptime, load, CPU counters, memory, disks and reboot flag and the names of unhealthy containers (empty if docker is absent). Sections start with a '##name' line. The update counts are what `apt-get upgrade --with-new-pkgs` would install now (a simulation, needs no root): phased Ubuntu updates and kept-back packages are not counted.
commands.script: echo '##hostname'; hostname; echo '##os'; cat /etc/os-release; echo '##uptime'; cat /proc/uptime; echo '##loadavg'; cat /proc/loadavg; echo '##nproc'; nproc; echo '##stat'; head -1 /proc/stat; echo '##meminfo'; grep -E '^(MemTotal|MemAvailable):' /proc/meminfo; echo '##df'; df -P -B1 -x tmpfs -x devtmpfs -x squashfs -x overlay -x efivarfs 2>/dev/null; echo '##system'; echo "vendor=$(cat /sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor 2>/dev/null)"; echo "product=$(cat /sys/class/dmi/id/product_name 2>/dev/null)"; echo "machine_id=$(cat /etc/machine-id 2>/dev/null)"; echo "kernel=$(uname -r)"; echo "boot_id=$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id 2>/dev/null)"; echo "time=$(date '+%s %z %Z')"; echo "ip=$(ip -4 route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i ~ /^src$/){print $(i+1); exit}}')"; T=$(timeout 3 tailscale ip -4 2>/dev/null | head -1); [ -n "$T" ] || T=$(ip -4 -o addr show dev tailscale0 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $4}' | cut -d/ -f1 | head -1); echo "tailscale_ip=$T"; echo '##reboot'; if [ -f /var/run/reboot-required ]; then echo yes; else echo no; fi; U=$(LC_ALL=C apt-get -s upgrade --with-new-pkgs 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^Inst [^ ]+ \['); echo '##updates'; echo "$U" | grep -c '^Inst'; echo '##security'; echo "$U" | grep -c -E -- '-security[], ]'; echo '##unhealthy'; docker ps --filter health=unhealthy --format '{{.Names}}' 2>/dev/null || true

commands.description: All containers (docker ps -a) plus one-shot resource stats for running ones. Compose stacks are derived from container labels.
commands.script: echo '##docker'; if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo ok; else echo missing; fi; echo '##ps'; docker ps -a --format '{{json .}}' 2>&1; echo '##stats'; docker stats --no-stream --format '{{json .}}' 2>&1 || true

commands.description: Read-only, light container check for background alerts: every container's id, name, state, status text (which carries the exit code: 'Exited (1) 2 hours ago'), compose project and Homepage bookmark address (for certificate checks). No `docker stats`, so it is fast. Errors are folded into stdout (2>&1) so a refused socket or a missing docker can be told apart from no containers. Ends with true.
docker start one container. {id} must match ^[0-9a-f]{12,64}$.
docker stop one container. {id} must match ^[0-9a-f]{12,64}$.
docker restart one container. {id} must match ^[0-9a-f]{12,64}$.
Follow one container's logs, starting with the last 100 lines. Run over a pseudo-terminal on its own connection; stop by sending Ctrl-C. {id} must match ^[0-9a-f]{12,64}$.

Packages apt can upgrade (from the local package cache; no root, no network), held packages, when the cache was last refreshed, and whether a reboot is pending. '##deferred' lists what apt would NOT install now, from a simulated `apt-get upgrade --with-new-pkgs` (no root needed): 'phased <name>' (Ubuntu's gradual rollout) or 'kept <name>' (needs a removal or is held).
commands.script: echo '##apt'; if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo ok; else echo missing; fi; echo '##upgradable'; apt list --upgradable 2>/dev/null; echo '##deferred'; LC_ALL=C apt-get -s upgrade --with-new-pkgs 2>/dev/null | awk '/^[^ ]/{s=""} /^(The following upgrades have been deferred due to phasing|Not upgrading yet due to phasing):/{s="phased ";next} /^(The following packages have been kept back|Not upgrading):/{s="kept ";next} s!=""{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) print s $i}'; echo '##held'; apt-mark showhold 2>/dev/null; echo '##refreshed'; stat -c %Y /var/lib/apt/periodic/update-success-stamp 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y /var/lib/apt/lists 2>/dev/null; echo '##reboot'; if [ -f /var/run/reboot-required ]; then echo yes; else echo no; fi

commands.description: Read-only storage reading of an Unraid server (detected from /etc/os-release ID unraid-os): array state and parity check progress from emhttp's var.ini, every array/pool/flash device (size, temperature, errors, filesystem use) from disks.ini, user shares from shares.ini, ZFS pool health, hwmon temperatures and fan speeds, the CPU model and the last parity checks. Reads what Unraid's own web UI already wrote, so no disk is spun up. Ends with true: missing files print nothing. Temperatures are read last, after a one-second pause and with shell builtins only, so the reading is not taken while this command's own ssh login and process starts are briefly loading the CPU (that made modern Intel package temperatures read 90-100 °C).
commands.script: echo '##unraid'; sed -n 's/^version="\(.*\)"$/\1/p' /etc/unraid-version 2>/dev/null; echo '##var'; grep -E '^(mdState|mdNumDisks|mdNumDisabled|mdNumInvalid|mdNumMissing|mdResync|mdResyncPos|mdResyncSize|mdResyncAction|mdResyncDt|mdResyncDb|sbSynced|sbSynced2|sbSyncErrs|sbSyncExit|fsState|shareCount)=' /var/local/emhttp/var.ini 2>/dev/null; echo '##disks'; grep -E '^\[|^(name|device|id|size|transport|rotational|spundown|status|temp|numErrors|type|fsType|fsStatus|fsMountpoint|fsSize|fsFree|fsUsed|devices|fsProfile)=' /var/local/emhttp/disks.ini 2>/dev/null; echo '##shares'; grep -E '^\[|^(name|comment|useCache|cachePool|free)=' /var/local/emhttp/shares.ini 2>/dev/null; echo '##zpool'; zpool list -H -o name,size,alloc,free,health 2>/dev/null; echo '##fans'; for h in /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*; do n=$(cat "$h/name" 2>/dev/null); for f in "$h"/fan*_input; do [ -r "$f" ] && echo "$n|$(cat "${f%_input}_label" 2>/dev/null)|$(cat "$f" 2>/dev/null)"; done; done; echo '##cpu'; grep -m1 '^model name' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2- | sed 's/^ *//'; echo '##parity'; tail -n 10 /boot/config/parity-checks.log 2>/dev/null; echo '##temps'; sleep 1; for h in /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*; do n=; read -r n 2>/dev/null < "$h/name"; for t in "$h"/temp*_input; do [ -r "$t" ] || continue; l=; read -r l 2>/dev/null < "${t%_input}_label"; v=; read -r v 2>/dev/null < "$t"; echo "$n|$l|$v"; done; done; true

commands.description: Read-only discovery of what runs on a server outside Docker: every loaded systemd service unit (system, and the ssh user's own `systemctl --user` units) with its state, boot setting, unit file, main PID, start time (monotonic, against ##uptime), memory and restart count; listening TCP sockets with their processes (ss -p shows only the ssh user's own processes unless it is root); and for each listening process its command line and cgroup, which ties a port to its unit or marks it as a process started by hand (a login session scope). Docker containers are left to the Docker screen. Ends with true: a server without systemd or ss prints empty sections.
commands.script: echo '##uptime'; cut -d' ' -f1 /proc/uptime; echo '##uid'; id -u; P=Id,Description,LoadState,ActiveState,SubState,Result,UnitFileState,FragmentPath,Type,MainPID,ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic,MemoryCurrent,NRestarts; echo '##system'; systemctl show --no-pager -p "$P" '*.service' 2>/dev/null; echo '##user'; systemctl --user show --no-pager -p "$P" '*.service' 2>/dev/null; echo '##listen'; ss -H -tlnp 2>/dev/null; echo '##procs'; for p in $(ss -H -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'pid=[0-9]*' | cut -d= -f2 | sort -un); do printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$p" "$(head -c 300 /proc/$p/cmdline 2>/dev/null | tr '\0\n\t' '   ')" "$(grep -m1 -E '^0::|name=systemd:' /proc/$p/cgroup 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f3)"; done; true

commands.description: docker compose pull for one stack: downloads newer images, changes no containers. {project} must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$. {dir} is the project's working directory, and {files} is `-f <path>` once per compose file, in label order (compose merges them in that order). All paths are absolute, from the project's labels, single-quoted for the shell (' becomes '\'').

docker compose up -d for one stack: recreates only containers whose image or config changed, starts stopped ones. {project} must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$. {dir} is the project's working directory, and {files} is `-f <path>` once per compose file, in label order (compose merges them in that order). All paths are absolute, from the project's labels, single-quoted for the shell (' becomes '\'').

docker compose restart for one stack: restarts every container without recreating it. {project} must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$. {dir} is the project's working directory, and {files} is `-f <path>` once per compose file, in label order. All paths are absolute, from the project's labels, single-quoted for the shell.

docker compose up -d --build for one stack: rebuilds images for services with a build section (from their Dockerfiles), then recreates the containers whose image or config changed. Services that only use pulled images are untouched. {project} must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$. {dir} is the project's working directory, and {files} is `-f <path>` once per compose file, in label order. All paths are absolute, from the project's labels, single-quoted for the shell.

docker compose up -d --build --no-deps for ONE service of a stack: rebuilds that service's image from its Dockerfile and recreates its container if it changed; its dependencies and the other services are untouched. {service} must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ and be a service of the stack (from the container's compose service label). Other placeholders as in compose_rebuild.

docker compose up -d --force-recreate for one stack: recreates every container. {project} must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$. {dir} is the project's working directory, and {files} is `-f <path>` once per compose file, in label order (compose merges them in that order). All paths are absolute, from the project's labels, single-quoted for the shell (' becomes '\'').
apt-get update: refresh the package lists. Installs nothing. Runs as root, or through `sudo -n` (never prompts) for other users; it fails with sudo's message if that is not allowed.
commands.script: if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then S=; else S='sudo -n'; fi; $S env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive LC_ALL=C apt-get update

commands.description: apt-get upgrade: install every available upgrade. Never installs new packages or removes any, and held packages stay. Keeps existing config files. Runs as root, or through `sudo -n` (never prompts) for other users; it fails with sudo's message if that is not allowed. --with-new-pkgs installs new dependencies (a new kernel's packages) but still never removes anything.
commands.script: if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then S=; else S='sudo -n'; fi; $S env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive LC_ALL=C apt-get upgrade --with-new-pkgs -y -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold

commands.description: apt-get install --only-upgrade for the named packages only (used for security updates). {packages} is a space-separated list; at most 200 names, each must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]+$. Runs as root, or through `sudo -n` (never prompts) for other users; it fails with sudo's message if that is not allowed.
commands.script: if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then S=; else S='sudo -n'; fi; $S env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive LC_ALL=C apt-get install --only-upgrade -y -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold {packages}

commands.description: Interactive shell in one container, run as the remote command of an ssh -t terminal tab (not through the transport). {id} must match ^[0-9a-f]{12,64}$.
commands.script: docker exec -it {id} sh -c 'if command -v bash >/dev/null 2>&1; then exec bash; else exec sh; fi'

commands.description: Pull Latest Image for a standalone container (one with no compose project label): downloads a newer copy of the image it runs. The container keeps the image it was created from; nothing restarts. {image} is the container's image reference from docker ps, only letters, digits and ._-/:@, not an image id (12 or 64 hex characters) and not starting with sha256:, and single-quoted for the shell.

Delete a standalone container (one with no compose project label): stops and removes it. {volumes} is empty or ` -v` (also remove its anonymous volumes). Named volumes, bind-mounted folders and the image are never removed. {id} must match ^[0-9a-f]{12,64}$.

Read one file of a stack (a compose file or <working_dir>/.env): missing, too large (over 65536 bytes), or its mtime, mode, owner, sha256 and base64 content. Read only. {file} is the quoted absolute path.
commands.script: F={file}; if [ ! -e "$F" ]; then echo '##missing'; exit 0; fi; if [ "$(stat -c %s "$F")" -gt 65536 ]; then echo '##toolarge'; exit 0; fi; echo '##meta'; stat -c '%Y %a %U:%G' "$F"; echo '##sha256'; sha256sum "$F" | cut -d' ' -f1; echo '##content'; base64 -w0 "$F"; echo

commands.description: Check new content for one stack file without changing anything: writes it to a temp file in the stack's folder and runs docker compose config -q with the temp file standing in for the edited file (or as --env-file for .env). Exit 0 = valid; otherwise the output holds compose's errors (e.g. 'yaml: line 5: ...'); exit 7 = the folder is not writable. {args} is -f for every compose file with the edited one replaced by "$T". All paths are absolute and single-quoted for the shell; {b64} is the file content base64-encoded and quoted.
commands.script: D={dir}; T=$(mktemp "$D/.rackoon-check.XXXXXX") || { echo '##cannot-write'; exit 7; }; trap 'rm -f "$T"' EXIT; echo {b64} | base64 -d > "$T"; docker compose -p {project} --project-directory "$D" {args} config -q 2>&1

commands.description: Save new content over one stack file: refuses if the file's sha256 no longer matches what was opened (exit 3, ##changed; {expect} is that check, or a not-exists check for a new file), validates with docker compose config (exit 4, ##invalid, nothing written), copies the old file to <file>.rackoon.bak, keeps owner and mode, then moves the new file into place atomically (##saved and the new sha256). Exit 7 = not writable. All paths are absolute and single-quoted for the shell; {b64} is the file content base64-encoded and quoted.
commands.script: F={file}; D={dir}; {expect}; T=$(mktemp "$D/.rackoon-save.XXXXXX") || { echo '##cannot-write'; exit 7; }; trap 'rm -f "$T"' EXIT; echo {b64} | base64 -d > "$T"; if ! OUT=$(docker compose -p {project} --project-directory "$D" {args} config -q 2>&1); then echo '##invalid'; echo "$OUT"; exit 4; fi; if [ -e "$F" ]; then chmod --reference="$F" "$T"; chown --reference="$F" "$T" 2>/dev/null; cp -p "$F" "$F.rackoon.bak" || { echo '##cannot-write'; exit 7; }; else chmod 600 "$T"; fi; mv -f "$T" "$F"; echo '##saved'; sha256sum "$F" | cut -d' ' -f1

commands.description: The guard {expect} is replaced with in file_write for a file that existed when it was opened: exit 3 and ##changed unless the file still has the sha256 it was opened with ({sha} is that hash, single-quoted).
The guard {expect} is replaced with in file_write for a file that did not exist when the editor started: exit 3 and ##changed if something is there now.

Check a NEW stack's files without creating anything in its real folder: writes compose.yaml (and .env, when {env} is the .env step) into a scratch folder from mktemp -d, runs docker compose config -q there, and removes the scratch folder on exit. {b64} is the compose file base64-encoded and quoted; {project} must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$. {env} is empty or `echo <base64> | base64 -d > "$T/.env"; `. Exit 7 = cannot create the scratch folder.
commands.script: T=$(mktemp -d) || { echo '##cannot-write'; exit 7; }; trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT; echo {b64} | base64 -d > "$T/compose.yaml"; {env}cd "$T" && docker compose -p {project} config -q 2>&1

commands.description: Create a new stack: refuses if {dir} already exists (exit 3, ##exists), creates {parent} if needed and then {dir} (exit 7 = not writable), writes compose.yaml (and .env with mode 600 when {env} is the .env step: `echo <base64> | base64 -d > "$D/.env" && chmod 600 "$D/.env" || exit 7; `, otherwise empty), checks it in place with docker compose config -q (exit 4, ##invalid), and on any failure removes the files and the folder it made. Success prints ##created. {dir} is <parent>/<name>; all paths are absolute and single-quoted for the shell. {b64} is the compose file base64-encoded and quoted.
commands.script: D={dir}; P={parent}; if [ -e "$D" ]; then echo '##exists'; exit 3; fi; mkdir -p "$P" && mkdir "$D" || { echo '##cannot-write'; exit 7; }; ok=; trap '[ -n "$ok" ] || { rm -f "$D/compose.yaml" "$D/.env"; rmdir "$D" 2>/dev/null; }' EXIT; echo {b64} | base64 -d > "$D/compose.yaml" || exit 7; {env}if ! OUT=$(cd "$D" && docker compose -p {project} config -q 2>&1); then echo '##invalid'; echo "$OUT"; exit 4; fi; ok=1; echo '##created'

commands.description: The text {env} is replaced with in stack_new_check when the new stack has a .env: writes the base64 content {envb64} to the scratch folder's .env before compose checks it.

The text {env} is replaced with in stack_create when the new stack has a .env: writes the base64 content {envb64} to the new folder's .env and makes it readable only by its owner (chmod 600); exit 7 if that fails.

Does the image exist in its registry, as seen from the server (so private registries it is logged in to work)? Prints found, timeout (20 s) or notfound; notfound also covers a registry that needs a login. {image} is a validated image name (letters, digits and . _ / : @ -), single-quoted.
commands.script: timeout 20 docker manifest inspect {image} >/dev/null 2>&1; case $? in 0) echo found;; 124) echo timeout;; *) echo notfound;; esac

commands.description: TCP ports with a listener on the server, one line per socket: the fourth column is the local address and the port follows its last colon. Used to tell whether a host port is free before adding a container.

Delete a stack: docker compose down --remove-orphans stops and removes its containers and the networks compose made (images are never removed). {volumes} is empty or ` -v` (also remove the named volumes the compose file declares). {folder} is empty, or the folder step: ` && cd / && { [ -f {file} ] || { echo '<missing>'; exit 6; }; } && { [ ! -L {dir} ] || { echo '<symlink>'; exit 6; }; } && R=$(readlink -f -- {dir}) && { case "$(readlink -f -- {file})" in "$R"/*) true;; *) echo '<outside>'; exit 6;; esac; } && { rm -rf -- {dir} || { [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ] && sudo -n rm -rf -- {dir}; } || { echo '<permissions>'; exit 6; }; }`. It runs only after down succeeded. Each guard has its own message and exit 6: the compose file is missing, the folder is itself a symlink, or the compose file's real path is not inside the folder's real path (a symlinked parent folder is fine and is deleted through); sudo -n is the second try for files a container created as root. The app offers it only for a folder that is not a system tree, mount point or home folder and that holds every compose file of the stack. {project} must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$; all paths are absolute and single-quoted for the shell.

The text {folder} is replaced with in compose_down when the stack's folder is deleted too. It runs only after `down` succeeded: leave /, then guard (each with its own message and exit 6, because the containers are gone by then): the stack's compose file {file} exists, the folder {dir} itself is not a symlink, and the compose file's real path lies inside the folder's real path (a symlinked PARENT such as /opt -> /mnt/data/opt is fine and is deleted through). Then rm -rf the folder, with sudo -n as a second try for files a container created as root.
commands.script: && cd / && { [ -f {file} ] || { echo 'The containers are removed, but the folder was left alone: its compose file is missing.'; exit 6; }; } && { [ ! -L {dir} ] || { echo 'The containers are removed, but the folder was left alone: it is a symbolic link.'; exit 6; }; } && R=$(readlink -f -- {dir}) && { case "$(readlink -f -- {file})" in "$R"/*) true;; *) echo 'The containers are removed, but the folder was left alone: its compose file is not inside it.'; exit 6;; esac; } && { rm -rf -- {dir} || { [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ] && sudo -n rm -rf -- {dir}; } || { echo 'The containers are removed, but the folder could not be deleted (permissions).'; exit 6; }; }

commands.description: The kernel's boot id: a random id that changes on every boot. Used after a reboot to tell the server has really restarted, not just kept its old connection.

Reboot the server in 2 seconds (so this ssh command can return and close cleanly). Runs as root or through sudo -n; if sudo would ask for a password it exits 5 with ##no-sudo and nothing is scheduled. The reboot is started with nohup so it survives the session ending.
commands.script: if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then S=; else S='sudo -n'; fi; $S true || { echo '##no-sudo'; exit 5; }; nohup sh -c "sleep 2; $S systemctl reboot" >/dev/null 2>&1 </dev/null & echo '##rebooting'

commands.description: The reboot for a user whose sudo wants a password, after `reboot` answered ##no-sudo. sudo -S reads the password from the command's standard input (the app writes it there, followed by a newline, and nowhere else: never in the command text), -p '' prints no prompt, and one sudo call does everything as root so no second sudo runs inside the delayed shell. sudo's messages go to stdout; any refusal (wrong password, not in sudoers, requiretty) exits 6 with ##sudo-failed and nothing is scheduled.
commands.script: sudo -S -p '' sh -c 'nohup sh -c "sleep 2; systemctl reboot" >/dev/null 2>&1 </dev/null & echo "##rebooting"' 2>&1 || { echo '##sudo-failed'; exit 6; }

commands.description: Put in front of an unchanged root script (apt_* and the command library's root entries, which use S='sudo -n') when the user gave a sudo password. {nonce} is 32 random lowercase hex characters, new for every attempt. `sudo -v` asks for the password once, before the script runs, with a prompt carrying the nonce (sudo-rs shows it as `[sudo: ##rackoon-sudo-<nonce>:] Password: `); the app types the password at that prompt only and hides its line. Then the ok marker is printed and the script's own `sudo -n` uses the session record `sudo -v` made. From the ok marker on, the app never types or looks for prompts again, so text the script prints (journal lines, user names) can't make it type the password. A second prompt before the ok marker means a wrong password: one Ctrl-C. The fail marker (exit 7) means sudo said no for another reason. mesg n stops other users on the server from writing into the session (wall/write) to fake a prompt or marker; stty -echo keeps stray input from being shown. A second prompt counts as a wrong password only if sudo said so first; otherwise it is another question (2FA, password change) and gets one Ctrl-C. The password is never part of a command.
commands.script: if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then mesg n 2>/dev/null; stty -echo 2>/dev/null; sudo -p '##rackoon-sudo-{nonce}:' -v || { echo '##rackoon-sudo-fail-{nonce}'; exit 7; }; fi; echo '##rackoon-sudo-ok-{nonce}';

commands.description: Wraps an action's command to stream its output live: stty sets the pty to the terminal that will show it ({cols}x{rows}), the command runs in a subshell, and its exit code is printed as a final ##rackoon-exit:<n> line (a streamed ssh gives output but no exit status). Used with a pty (ssh -tt) so docker compose draws its normal progress.
commands.script: stty cols {cols} rows {rows} 2>/dev/null; ( {command} ); rk=$?; echo; echo "##rackoon-exit:$rk"

commands.description: List one folder for the Files screen. {dir} is an absolute path, single-quoted. Exit 3: the folder doesn't exist; exit 4: it isn't readable. Output is NUL separated: the folder's real path (symlinks resolved), then eight fields per entry: type (f d l ...), type after following a link (d for a link to a folder, N broken), size in bytes, modified as epoch seconds, permissions as ls prints them, owner, name, link target (empty unless a link). Needs GNU find. NUL separation keeps any file name intact. The app shows at most 5000 entries.
The ssh user's home folder as an absolute real path, where the Files screen starts.

Upload one file: the content arrives on stdin. {dest} and {tmp} are absolute single-quoted paths (tmp is `.<name>.rackoon-part` beside dest) and {bytes} is the exact size being sent. Written to tmp first and moved into place only if tmp is exactly {bytes} long (a cancelled or dropped upload looks like a normal end of input to cat, so without the check a half file would be moved into place); an existing file keeps its owner and mode; a folder with that name is refused (exit 5).
commands.script: D={dest}; T={tmp}; if [ -d "$D" ]; then echo 'A folder with that name already exists.' >&2; exit 5; fi; cat > "$T" || { rm -f -- "$T"; exit 1; }; if [ "$(wc -c < "$T")" -ne {bytes} ]; then rm -f -- "$T"; echo 'The upload was interrupted, so nothing was changed.' >&2; exit 1; fi; if [ -e "$D" ]; then chmod --reference="$D" "$T" 2>/dev/null; chown --reference="$D" "$T" 2>/dev/null; fi; mv -f -- "$T" "$D" || { rm -f -- "$T"; exit 1; }

commands.description: Upload a folder: a tar stream on stdin holding {src}/... is received into a scratch folder ({tmpdir}, a mktemp template inside the destination folder), checked to be exactly {bytes} long (else nothing is touched, exit 1), unpacked, then moved to {dest}; if {dest} is already a folder its contents are merged in. Files are owned by the ssh user (--no-same-owner). The scratch folder is always removed.
commands.script: T=$(mktemp -d {tmpdir}) || exit 1; mkdir "$T/x"; cat > "$T/in.tar"; if [ "$(wc -c < "$T/in.tar")" -ne {bytes} ]; then echo 'The upload was interrupted, so nothing was changed.' >&2; rc=1; else tar -xf "$T/in.tar" -C "$T/x" --no-same-owner; rc=$?; if [ $rc -eq 0 ]; then if [ -d {dest} ]; then cp -a -- "$T"/x/{src}/. {dest}/; else mv -- "$T"/x/{src} {dest}; fi; rc=$?; fi; fi; rm -rf -- "$T"; exit $rc

commands.description: Download one file: the content leaves on stdout. {path} is absolute and single-quoted.

Download a folder as a tar stream of its contents on stdout. {path} is the absolute single-quoted folder; tar changes into it, which follows a symlink to a folder (links inside stay links). The app unpacks it into a folder named after the entry.
Create one folder. {path} is absolute and single-quoted. Refuses a name that is taken (exit 5); never creates parents.
commands.script: if [ -e {path} ] || [ -L {path} ]; then echo 'That name is already taken.' >&2; exit 5; fi; mkdir -- {path}

commands.description: Rename or move within one folder. {from} and {to} are absolute single-quoted paths. Refuses when {to} exists (exit 5).
commands.script: if [ -e {to} ] || [ -L {to} ]; then echo 'That name is already taken.' >&2; exit 5; fi; mv -- {from} {to}

commands.description: Delete one file, or a symlink itself (a link is never followed).

Delete a folder and everything in it. Offered only for folders that are not system trees, mount points, home folders or shallower than three levels (checked by the app and again before the command is built).
